chapters.F: Four foundations: token cost, context window, errors, keys.
chapters.D1: Choose the simplest architecture that fits the steps.
chapters.D2: Lowest tier, tuned effort, counted tokens, cached prefix.
chapters.D3: Scope tools, trace hops, ground answers, defer catalogs.
chapters.D4: Measure outcomes, diagnose the layer, batch what can wait.
chapters.D5: Enforce in code, approve the irreversible, confirm coverage.
chapters.D6: Turn words into metrics, record decisions, pass the gates.
chapters.D7: Settings and hooks enforce. CLAUDE.md suggests.

exam_rules: Enforce controls in code. Prompts guide the model.
Pick the lowest tier that clears the measured quality floor.
Count tokens with the model you will call.
Price each option per completed task, and date the price.
Scope the tools before you add monitoring.
Cache the stable prefix. Move variables after the breakpoint.
Batch the work that no user waits for.
Trace every model and tool hop with one trace ID.
Approve irreversible actions first. Review reversible actions after.
Confirm feature coverage before regulated data reaches the API.

units.F1: Rate per token class, sum the classes, then times volume.
units.F2: Fit the window first. Then choose what enters it.
units.F3: Retry 429 and 5xx with backoff. Fix 400 and 401 first.
units.F4: Scoped, time-limited, identity-backed key. Never in the prompt.
units.D1.1: Fixed mapping: code. Open input: Claude plus a code check.
units.D1.2: The application owns history, retries, and stop reasons.
units.D1.3: Known steps: tool-use loop. Open steps: agent loop.
units.D1.4: Independent scoped work only. One lead owns the merge.
units.D1.5: Split at independent seams. Check the merge in code.
units.D1.6: Unit cost from published rates, times expected volume.
units.D2.1: Lowest tier that clears the measured floor. Then tune effort.
units.D2.2: Role and output rules in the prompt. Access rules in code.
units.D2.3: Three to five diverse examples. Measure before adding more.
units.D2.4: Count with the model you call. Budget before you send.
units.D2.5: Breakpoint on the last block shared by every cached request.
units.D3.1: Remove the tools the task does not need. Then monitor.
units.D3.2: Per-user credential when the audit must name the person.
units.D3.3: Smallest model and effort that pass quality and latency.
units.D3.4: Trace every model and tool hop with one trace ID.
units.D3.5: Search result blocks when answers need checkable sources.
units.D3.6: Keywords for exact terms. Semantic for paraphrase. Filters for access.
units.D3.7: Messages API and remote MCP: connector, tool calls only.
units.D3.8: Ten or more tools, or over 10k tokens: defer the definitions.
units.D4.1: Business outcome is primary. Proxy scores are diagnostics.
units.D4.2: Build from production traffic. Add production edge cases.
units.D4.3: One arm per unit. Compare on the primary metric and threshold.
units.D4.4: Earliest changed block in the prefix. Move variables after it.
units.D4.5: Work that nobody waits for: batch. User waits: synchronous.
units.D4.6: Show spend beside completed tasks. Alert on cost per task.
units.D5.1: Screen untrusted text. Enforce authorization in code.
units.D5.2: Every claim needs a source quote, or it goes.
units.D5.3: Irreversible action: approve before. Reversible: review after.
units.D5.4: ZDR per organization. Check feature coverage before regulated data.
units.D5.5: Policy and examples in the prompt. A schema constrains the verdict.
units.D6.1: Each adjective becomes a metric, a threshold, and an owner.
units.D6.2: Compare cost per completed task. Date every price.
units.D6.3: Read usage and cost on a schedule. Compare with thresholds.
units.D6.4: Record each decision with alternatives, owner, and evidence.
units.D6.5: A phase fails: return to the earliest skipped gate.
units.D7.1: Control: permission rule or hook. Convention: CLAUDE.md.
units.D7.3: Run the built-in check for the symptom first.
